title: Linux tools and reproducible engineering
objectives: Find files and logs confidently, compile a program, preserve a change in Git and capture enough context for someone else to reproduce a failure.
references: [GIT] Git official tutorial. [GCC-WARN] GCC warning options. [LD] GNU linker scripts.

title: C memory ownership and defined behavior
objectives: Track object lifetime and bounds, explain pointer declarations, distinguish language behavior categories and choose qualifiers correctly.
references: [C11] WG14 N1570 public draft. [GCC13] GCC 13.3 instrumentation. [GCC-VOL] GCC volatile access. [K-VOL] Linux volatile guidance.

title: Data structures and defensive protocols
objectives: Implement a bounded ring buffer and state machine, define a binary wire format and recover from corrupted or incomplete input.
references: [READ] Linux read semantics. [WRITE] Linux write semantics. B01 and B03 contain original protocol contracts and tests.

title: Build systems linking and C++ ownership
objectives: Inspect ELF objects, diagnose link/runtime mismatches and use a small RAII wrapper without copying an owning resource.
references: [LD] GNU ld linker scripts. [CMAKE] CMake 3.28 toolchain manual. [CPP] C++ Core Guidelines. [CLOSE] Linux close semantics.

title: Processor and operating system foundations
objectives: Explain virtual memory, privilege, scheduling and device access, and separate application processors from microcontrollers.
references: [DMA] Linux DMA mapping guide. [CMSIS] Arm CMSIS startup. [NVIC] Arm NVIC documentation. [KLOCK] Linux lock types.

title: Linux I/O processes and event loops
objectives: Write correct partial-I/O loops, manage child processes and implement bounded timeouts and graceful termination.
references: [READ] read manual. [WRITE] write manual. [EPOLL] epoll_ctl manual. [SIGNAL] signal-safety manual. [PROC] proc_pid_stat manual.

title: Concurrency synchronization and IPC
objectives: Protect invariants, use condition variables correctly, reason about deadlock and choose an IPC mechanism for a measured need.
references: [COND] POSIX condition-wait manual. [GCC13] GCC sanitizer options. [KLOCK] Kernel lock context comparison.

title: Cross compilation boot and device tree
objectives: Build for a foreign target, identify boot-stage evidence and describe hardware with validated bindings.
references: [CMAKE] CMake toolchains. [QEMU-USER] QEMU userspace. [QEMU-VIRT] Generic virt machine. [DT] Linux device tree. [DTSCHEMA] Binding schemas.

title: Kernel execution contexts and resource lifetimes
objectives: Choose context-appropriate allocation and locks, reason about deferred work and prevent teardown races.
references: [KALLOC] Kernel allocation guide. [KLOCK] Kernel locking. [WORK] Workqueues. [DRIVER] Driver model. [RCU] RCU fundamentals.

title: Character and platform drivers
objectives: Implement an educational character interface, define blocking and poll semantics, and choose a standard subsystem for real hardware.
references: [UACCESS] Kernel uaccess API. [DRIVER] Linux driver model. [GPIO] GPIO consumers. [IIO] Industrial I/O subsystem.

title: Peripheral buses sensor subsystems DMA and power
objectives: Read a datasheet into an interface contract, select a subsystem and explain data, DMA and power lifetimes.
references: [IIO] Linux IIO. [DMA] Linux DMA mapping. [RPM] Runtime PM. [GPIO] GPIO consumer rules. A01 provides its exact device datasheet.

title: Bare metal startup peripherals and faults
objectives: Explain reset-to-main, link memory correctly and design bounded peripheral handling and watchdog supervision.
references: [CMSIS] Arm startup contract. [NVIC] Arm interrupt controller APIs. [NUCLEO] ST board documentation. [LD] Linker scripts.

title: RTOS scheduling and Linux to MCU communication
objectives: Use tasks and queues, analyze timing and priority inversion, and make an MCU communication boundary recoverable.
references: [FREERTOS-MUTEX] FreeRTOS mutex documentation. [NVIC] Arm interrupt rules. I05 includes its exact RTOS source and port references.

title: Buildroot Yocto and image maintenance
objectives: Choose the build-system scope, package a service and preserve a reproducible image configuration.
references: [BUILDROOT] Official manual and pinned release-local manual. [YOCTO-HOST] Yocto 5.0.9 requirements. [YOCTO-SBOM] Yocto SPDX generation. I04 includes exact layer/recipe references.

title: Debugging tracing and performance
prerequisites: M06 M07; M09 for kernel portions
objectives: Form falsifiable bug hypotheses, interpret crash evidence and measure latency without confusing averages with guarantees.
references: [GDB] GDB backtraces. [FTRACE] Kernel ftrace. [KASAN] KASAN. [KCSAN] KCSAN. [GCC13] GCC sanitizers.

title: Persistence security and reliable updates
objectives: Make configuration writes recoverable, distinguish update trust from boot trust and test rollback state transitions.
references: [UBOOT] U-Boot verified boot. [RAUC] RAUC basics. [YOCTO-SBOM] SBOM generation. [FSYNC] fsync durability. [RENAME] rename semantics.

title: Integration testing and capstone engineering
objectives: Turn requirements into acceptance tests, integrate earlier work and present evidence with clearly bounded claims.
references: [KUNIT] Kernel unit testing. C01 and C02 provide original requirements and acceptance tests. Project-specific sources govern actual hardware contracts.

title: AI assisted learning and embedded inference
objectives: Use AI to improve reasoning without losing independent competence, and evaluate a small inference extension against a non-AI baseline.
references: [LITERT] Google LiteRT for Microcontrollers. [ONNX] ONNX Runtime quantization. Core engineering contracts use the sources in the relevant preceding modules.
